method: For each of 5 iteration-1 BASELINE outputs, spawn one subagent that loads the simplify skill and applies its three-angle review framework (reuse / quality / efficiency) to the entire file. Compare findings vs the ground truth identified by hand in iteration-1's REPORT.md.

evals.name: fastapi-auth-baseline-review
evals.hand_findings_summary: verbose but technically correct; no specific bugs flagged
highlight_finds_beyond_hand_review: Per-request httpx.AsyncClient (should be shared via FastAPI lifespan) — real performance issue
3 identical 401 raises + 2 identical 502 raises → consolidate into helper functions
Missing `from exc` on 6 re-raises (broken exception chains lose original traceback)
tuple[str, int] return from _issue_jwt is parameter sprawl
Unvalidated int() env cast crashes at first request, not at config load
evals.decision_brief_quality: Recommended Option A — 7 consensus items only. Skipped single-reviewer opinion calls. Right calibration.

evals.name: data-cleaning-baseline-review
highlight_finds_beyond_hand_review: Naive datetime.now() vs tz-aware concern flagged but correctly deferred to Option B (needs caller context)
Testability: injectable clock for unit tests
evals.decision_brief_quality: Recommended Option A — vectorized fix only. Surfaced testability + tz concerns as Option B without forcing them. Right calibration.

evals.name: async-cache-baseline-review
evals.hand_findings_summary: sync requests.get in async, time.sleep blocks event loop, asyncio.run inside async fn
highlight_finds_beyond_hand_review: Thundering herd: no in-flight Task dedup — N concurrent requests for same URL all hit upstream
Unbounded cache growth: no eviction policy
Constant backoff with no jitter — synchronizes retry storms
No connection pooling without shared httpx.AsyncClient
Suggested industry-standard alternatives: tenacity for retries, async_lru.alru_cache for caching
evals.decision_brief_quality: Recommended Option B (full rewrite) over Option A (surgical patch) because the function is broken at runtime and a surgical fix leaves an async fn that still blocks the loop. Correct judgment.

evals.name: stub-todo-baseline-review
highlight_finds_beyond_hand_review: Return type should be NoReturn not None — functions that always raise have semantic meaning
`from __future__ import annotations` is dead — no forward references in this file
Hardcoded function name in error message is rename-unsafe (traceback already names the function)
Correctly REJECTED extracting a _stub() helper as YAGNI at N=2 — didn't manufacture an abstraction
evals.decision_brief_quality: Recommended Option A — consensus items + cheap one-liners. Skipped speculative refactoring. Right calibration.

evals.name: type-safe-cache-baseline-review
evals.hand_findings_summary: model defaults handled the prompt correctly; nothing to flag
evals.decision_brief_quality: Recommended SKIP — explicitly cited Phase 5 of the skill ('If the code was already clean, say so — don't manufacture findings'). No false positives.

headline_findings: The simplify skill catches every bug we found by hand AND surfaces 6.3× more findings on average (44 simplify vs 7 hand-found).

Eval-3 (the file with 3 runtime bugs) was the critical test. Simplify caught all 3 PLUS flagged 4 production concerns (thundering herd, unbounded growth, no jitter, no connection pooling) and proposed industry-standard libraries (tenacity, async_lru).
Eval-5 (already-clean code) correctly returned ZERO findings — the skill honored its Phase 5 'don't manufacture findings' rule. No false positives.

Decision-brief calibration is excellent. 4/5 reviews recommended Option A (consensus-only) which kept fixes tight. Eval-3 correctly escalated to Option B (full rewrite) because the function is broken at runtime.
Single-reviewer findings (judgment calls) were surfaced as Option B but not forced — exactly the skill's intended behavior for taste calls.

comparison_to_iteration_1.iteration_1_question: Does the python-rules skill prevent slop at generation time?
comparison_to_iteration_1.iteration_2_question: Does the simplify skill catch slop AFTER it's been generated?
comparison_to_iteration_1.iteration_2_answer: Yes — caught 100% of hand-found bugs + 6.3× more nuanced findings, with zero false positives on already-clean code.

what_this_validates: The TWO-LAYER architecture works: python-rules prevents at the source, simplify catches what slips through.

The LLM-intelligent layer (simplify) is substantively MORE thorough than rule-based detection — it catches design issues (thundering herd, connection pooling, NoReturn semantics) that no static lint rule can express.
The skill's decision-brief format produces well-calibrated recommendations — neither under-flagging (missed eval-3's runtime bug) nor over-flagging (eval-5 correctly skipped).
Phase 5's 'don't manufacture findings' rule is respected in practice — eval-5 returned cleanly.
limitations: Single-pass review on each file — we didn't test the iterative 'fix → re-scan → re-review' loop the skill describes.

Subagents applied the three angles sequentially in-process rather than spawning real parallel Task subagents (we said 'don't spawn sub-subagents' to keep the test tractable). Production use of /aidoctor:simplify in Claude Code would spawn 3 parallel reviewers per the skill's Phase 2.
5 evals is a small N. A larger corpus (50-100 real-world Python files) would give more confidence in the false-positive rate.
We tested simplify on iteration-1 BASELINES (intentionally lower-quality code). Should also test on already-good code to confirm the 'no manufactured findings' behavior holds across diverse inputs.
